checks: Mouse pickup readies the wooden spoon at the pan, then physically carries it from beside the pan to the pot without using a tool menu or changing cooking evidence.
Fork and spatula route to their correct cookware, frame their native gesture, and leave exact food, water, heat, time and logs unchanged.
A spatula carried from the rack performs a full slide, lift, turn and lower gesture; only that completed cooking movement records one turn.
Wrong cookware, a tap, and release away from cookware return the utensil without equipping a mode or recording an action.
Escape and an external heat change cancel a carried tool; the heat change produces its own single log with no stray pickup or cooking action.
A learner can inspect a utensil before the recipe is ready; recipe prerequisites remain truthful in both the scene and accessible chooser.
Keyboard users ready the same physical spatula and open its existing piece controls without creating cooking evidence during navigation.
Finished cooks and historical replay lock native pickup and keyboard ready buttons while keeping the rack camera available.
Real phone touch carries the masher from its visible hook to the pan and frames the tomato gesture, with a preview only during pickup.
The picked-up masher completes a real press, lift and release on the phone, conserving the piece’s finite juice and recording exactly one cooking action.
Touch cancellation returns the tool; reload restores the cook and starts with utensils on their hooks without persisting presentation as recipe evidence.
Drop routing follows the wide four-serving pan to its trivet without moving it or recording an action.
The rack chooser fits 320px, retains visible keyboard focus and usable controls, and passes forced-color accessibility checks.
